key_insight: Integrating uncertainty estimates from an nnU-Net segmentation model with a budget-aware selection strategy lets clinicians prioritize a small subset of auto-segmentations for review while catching most clinically relevant errors.
problem_solved: How to reliably flag where automated radiotherapy CTV segmentations might be wrong so limited expert QA time is used where it matters most, especially for complex treatments like TMLI.
method: Compute per-voxel and per-structure uncertainty from an nnU-Net segmentation model to estimate likely errors.
Rank slices/structures/patients by predicted uncertainty-derived error and select a fixed review budget (number of slices/regions) to present to clinicians.
Evaluate budget-aware QA performance on TMLI cases, measuring error detection vs reviewer effort trade-offs.
impact: Provides a practical workflow for deploying auto-segmentation in radiotherapy by focusing human effort on the most uncertain (and thus most error-prone) regions, improving safety and efficiency in clinical QA.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input CT → nnU-Net segmentation → uncertainty map → budgeted selection → clinician review
CT slice overlay heatmap showing uncertainty hotspots and corresponding segmentation errors
Curve/chart: fraction of errors detected versus review budget (resource vs coverage trade-off)
Bar chart: time saved or reductions in slices reviewed per patient while maintaining high error detection
paper_title: Budget-Aware Uncertainty for Radiotherapy Segmentation QA Using nnU-Net
paper_authors: Ricardo Coimbra Brioso, Lorenzo Mondo, Damiano Dei, Nicola Lambri, Pietro Mancosu
